title: 0.12.0 release candidate 1 breaks some MacOS keys (like [] {}) on Portuguese Layout
body:
Hi,

Trying 0.12.0 release candidate 1 on MacOS 12.6.3

The change:

alt_send_esc is now always set to true

reintroduced the problem described on #2280

using: 

option_as_alt: OnlyLeft

I can use the correct emacs keys on the terminal but I cannot type [] {} and some others from Portuguese keyboard layout that are typed using option and shift+option exactly like described on #2280 (that was solved by using alt_send_esc = false)

Thanks in advance

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
On Emacs I cannot type some of the keys ([ ] { } @) at all!

It worked before with alt_sed_esc = false and

    { key: Key8, mods: Alt|Shift, chars: "\x7B" } # {
    { key: Key9, mods: Alt|Shift, chars: "\x7D" } # }
    { key: Key8, mods: Alt, chars: "\x5B" } # [
    { key: Key9, mods: Alt, chars: "\x5D" } # ]
    { key: Key2, mods: Alt, chars: "\x40" } # @


Directly on the terminal I can type [ and ] by pressing the key 3 times ... 
{  } and @ work

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I recommend picking `None` or `Both` for now. `OnlyLeft` and `OnlyRight` will still send escape for both alt keys which is something that will get fixed in a future update.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 Thank's for you answer and your fantastic work on alacritty!

Unfortunately this makes alacritty completely unusable with Emacs for me and I guess for at least all international MacOS users.

- With `None` I would have to use ESC for meta instead of option and it would break my muscle memory (and of the majority of the users)
- With `Both` I can't type '[', '[', '{', '}' and '@' and I'm a developer :)

After several years happily using alacritty I'll have to search for another terminal ... I was having problems with 0.11 (the #62 ones) and was hoping they would be solved with 0.12 but I got bigger ones :)

>With None I would have to use ESC for meta instead of option and it would break my muscle memory (and of the majority of the users)

None is exactly as `alt_send_esc` before.

Yeah macOS has broken input model and there's no macOS developers who care. There's always an option to use US or ABC layouts which work just fine with new options.

Or you wait for 0.13 where it'll be solved.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant2 thank's for you answer

> None is exactly as alt_send_esc before.

Yes .. But I need `alt_send_esc = false` like it was possible before ... (check #2280)

> Or you wait for 0.13 where it'll be solved.

Yes I will return to alacritty for sure in 0.13! But meanwhile I will have to use another one (using iterm2 now)

EDIT: even solved with 0.13 .. for me the solution I had with `alt_send_esc = false`  + extra keys definitions was a lot better than having to use `OnlyLeft` and having to use left option for meta and right option to type those extra characters (not natural for me ..)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
>EDIT: even solved with 0.13 .. for me the solution I had with alt_send_esc = false + extra keys definitions was a lot better than having to use OnlyLeft and having to use left option for meta and right option to type those extra characters (not natural for me ..)

How does this work with e.g. iterm/terminal.app? It just no-one cares or uses macOS among alacritty contributors, so it's hard to figure out how this setting should behave. Most of the time it's just macOS has really bad input model for layouts other than US/ABS. Because with US layout I'm pretty sure you can input everything you want via the Alt key or you can have multiple keyboard layouts (it just happened that your native language has similar alphabet to English, but in reality you can't even input `Alt + [` for example, because you already use `Alt` to input `[`, so you're sort of limited from the start).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant2 with iterm2 was easy and fast:

First define what left option should do:

![Captura de ecrã 2023-02-20, às 00 47 32](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180825/219986310-4ce31077-47a6-46d8-b80d-27cef200105c.png)

Then define some keys to create some exceptions and for those extra keys accessed with option and shift+option

![Captura de ecrã 2023-02-20, às 00 48 15](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180825/219986321-9ceec30c-c3bb-4af8-89f2-640f08b0e68d.png)

A little similar to what I did before on alacritty:

`alt_send_esc = false`

and


{ key: Key8, mods: Alt|Shift, chars: "\x7B" } # {
{ key: Key9, mods: Alt|Shift, chars: "\x7D" } # }
{ key: Key8, mods: Alt, chars: "\x5B" } # [
{ key: Key9, mods: Alt, chars: "\x5D" } # ]
{ key: Key2, mods: Alt, chars: "\x40" } # @


and it worked like a charm ... before 0.11

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Are you aware that you can do exactly that with alacritty? You have `ReceivedChar` binding just fine to circumvent that? So you bind `Alt + Shift + 8` to do `ReceivedChar` and it'll be bypassed.

Are your bindings section not working or I don't understand that? Like it should work just fine now...

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: I know that those bindings broke with `0.11` but they should be fixed with new options in `0.12`.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Are your bindings section not working or I don't understand that? Like it should work just fine now...

those key bindings are working well! The problem is that `option` is not being interpreted as meta in Emacs ... `ESC` is

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: But `OptionAsAlt::Both/Left/Right` should produce `\x1b` for such keys, when pressing e.g. `Alt + a`? So if you type `Alt + a` you should get `^[a`. (you can test in shell by running `cat` and typing in to it with alt).

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: I'm pretty sure that the actual input from such keys should be exactly the same between iterm's option you specify and the one we have(I've tested it to be the same with US layout).

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Also, are you sure that you're adding it correctly.

```
window:
    option_as_alt: OnlyLeft
```

participant2

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: What keybindings are not working for you inside the `emacs`? It seems like `ESC` is correctly send by alacritty now with your layout?

But something as changed ... because It worked before like I had and not only for me .. for a lot of others and other languages .. like you can see here:

https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/wiki/Keyboard-mappings

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Yeah, the keyboard keys that you get might actually got changed in upstream library. I'll try to write up a release note about that. It won't be an issue with `0.13` where all the keybinding code will be changed and the way you bind them.

I'll try to write up a release note notice on how to proceed with the update, since as you may see you have the exact same experience as with iterm2 wrt `Alt` now, it just you bind the wrong thing.

Thank you very much for your help and your time! I'm very happy! I can keep using alacritty without having to wait for 0.13! :)
